mainTopic: Why the opening משנה of נדרים lists all four kinds of כינויים, why חרמים comes before שבועות, and the משנה's style of explaining ידות before כינויים
overview: The גמרא opens by asking why the first משנה of נדרים lists כינויים for all four categories (נדרים, חרמים, שבועות, נזירות), while the משנה in נזיר lists only its own topic. The answer is that נדר and שבועה are written together in the תורה, so the משנה mentions both, and once it lists two it lists all four. The גמרא then asks why שבועות doesn't come right after נדרים. The answer is that נדרים and חרמים both make an object forbidden, while in a שבועה the person forbids himself from the object. Next, the גמרא notes that the משנה opens with כינויים but its first example is a case of ידות, which it never introduced. It answers that words are missing: the משנה should also say that ידות of vows are like vows. Since ידות were mentioned last, the משנה explains them first, and the גמרא proves this style from three משניות in שבת. Five other משניות explain their first item first, and the גמרא answers that this happens when there are many cases. The amud ends with a challenge from the משנה about an animal going out on שבת, which has only two sides yet starts with the first. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does our משנה list all four categories?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the opening משנה of נדרים lists כינויים for every category, while the opening משנה of נזיר lists only נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "All substitutes for vows are like vows." Why does the משנה in נזיר not list all of them, while the משנה in נדרים does list all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the משנה. It asks why this משנה covers more topics than just vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת נדרים is about vows, so we would expect its משנה to mention only כינויי נדרים, the way מסכת נזיר mentions only כינויי נזירות. Instead, our משנה also lists חרמים, שבועות and נזירות. The גמרא wants to know why the two מסכתות are different.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute words for the standard vow language
What is different? (asking why two cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: GEMARA: "All substitutes for vows are like vows,"
what is different regarding נזיר
phrases.notes: He's pointing to the first משנה of מסכת נזיר, which lists only כינויי נזירות.

phrases.english: that it does not teach all of them,
and what is different regarding נדרים
that it teaches all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי נָזִיר דְּלָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה of נדרים lists all four categories of כינויים while נזיר lists only one

steps.title: Vows and oaths are written together in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: Because נדר and שבועה appear side by side in the פסוק, the משנה mentions both. Once it lists two, it lists all four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because vow and oath are written next to each other, it teaches two. Since it already teaches two, it teaches all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The תורה puts נדר and שבועה together, so the משנה does the same, and then it rounds out the list with all the categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (במדבר 30:3) says "a man who vows a vow or swears an oath," joining נדר and שבועה. That gives the משנה a reason to include שבועות. Once it is already going beyond its own topic, it simply lists every category. נזיר has no such pairing, so its משנה stays with its own topic.

phrases.english: Because vow and oath
are written next to each other
it teaches two,
and since it teaches two,
it teaches all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּנֶדֶר וּשְׁבוּעָה כְּתִיבִי גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק pairs נדר with שבועה, so the משנה includes שבועות. Having gone to two categories, it includes all four.

steps.title: Then oaths should come right after vows
steps.stepSummary: If שבועה is included only because it is paired with נדר, the משנה should list כינויי שבועות right after נדרים, not after חרמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach substitutes for oaths right after vows!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If oaths are in the list because they go with vows, why does the משנה put חרמים between them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given in step 2 links שבועה directly to נדר. But the order in the משנה is נדרים, חרמים, שבועות, נזירות. That order seems to ignore the very link that explained why שבועות was included.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach! (a challenge to the order or wording)

phrases.english: Then let it teach substitutes for oaths
right after vows!
phrases.notes: In the משנה, חרמים comes between נדרים and שבועות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a consequence of the answer in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the list in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שבועה is included because it is paired with נדר, it should appear right next to נדר.

steps.title: Vows and חרמים both forbid an object
steps.stepSummary: נדרים and חרמים are grouped together because both make an object forbidden. A שבועה is different: the person forbids himself from the object.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught vows, where an object becomes forbidden to a person, it also taught חרמים, where an object becomes forbidden to a person. This leaves out an oath, where the person forbids himself from the object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the order of the list. חרמים goes with נדרים because the two work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדר or a חרם, the forbidden status sits on the object itself. With a שבועה, the obligation sits on the person, who binds himself not to use it. Because they work the same way, נדר and חרם are grouped together first, and שבועה comes after.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it already (taught one thing, it taught a similar one)
Dedications (חרם), which make an object forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר (and a חרם) forbids the object to the person. A שבועה makes the person forbid himself from the object.
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference between a נדר and a שבועה, object versus person, is a basic idea that comes up again and again throughout מסכת נדרים.

phrases.english: Since it taught vows
where an object becomes forbidden to him,
it also taught חרמים,
where an object becomes forbidden to him.
This excludes an oath,
where he forbids himself from the object.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא נְדָרִים דְּמִיתְּסַר חֶפְצָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the order by grouping categories that share the same legal mechanism
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבועה should come right after נדר because the פסוק pairs them
steps.terutzMaskana: חרם is placed with נדר because both forbid an object. שבועה, which works on the person, comes after.

steps.title: The משנה opened with כינויים but explains ידות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה begins with כינויים, yet its first example ("I am מודר from you") is a case of ידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It opened with substitutes, "All substitutes for vows," and then explains handles: one who says to his friend "I am avowed from you"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about how the משנה is arranged. The opening line talks about כינויים, but the next line gives an example of ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כינויים are substitute words for a vow, while ידות are partial phrases that "hold onto" a vow. The משנה's opening line announces one topic, then immediately gives an example of a different one. That seems out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "handles": partial or shortened vow expressions
I am forbidden by vow from you

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up כינויים and ידות. כינויים are replacement words for the vow language. ידות are incomplete phrases that still count as a vow.

phrases.english: It opened with substitutes
"All substitutes for vows,"
and then explains handles:
one who says to his friend "I am avowed from you"!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּתַח בְּכִינּוּיִין ״כָּל כִּנּוּיַי נְדָרִים״, וּמְפָרֵשׁ יָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the style of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The arrangement of the משנה's opening lines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that opens with כינויים should explain כינויים first, not jump to ידות.

steps.title: Did the משנה forget to mention ידות?
steps.stepSummary: A second problem: the משנה gives an example of ידות without ever stating a general rule about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: did it forget handles?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second difficulty to the first one. The משנה never introduced ידות at all, yet it gives an example of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with a general statement about כינויים in all four categories. It has no matching statement that ידות count as vows. So the example of ידות seems to come out of nowhere, as if the תנא forgot to introduce them.

phrases.english: And furthermore: did it forget handles?!
phrases.notes: אִינְּשִׁי means "forgot." The משנה never wrote a general line like "all ידות of vows are like vows."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difficulty to the question of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the משנה leaves out any general statement about ידות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives an example of ידות without first introducing ידות as a category.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: ידות also count like vows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does deal with ידות. Some words are missing, and the full text should say that both כינויים and ידות are like נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about ידות. Some words are missing. This is what it means: all substitute words for vows count like vows, and ידות of vows also count like vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the questions from Steps 5 and 6 by saying the משנה left out a line. Once we fill it in, the משנה states a rule about ידות before it gives the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the משנה gave an example of ידות ("I am מודר from you") without first stating a rule about ידות. The answer is that a rule about ידות belongs in the משנה but was left out of the written text. With that line put back, the example has a rule to illustrate.

keyTerms.meaning: It is dealing with them (here: the ידות)
The text is missing something; words need to be filled in
And this is what it is teaching
Substitute words for the language of vows
Partial or shortened phrases that are clearly tied to a full vow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up כינויים and ידות. כינויים are substitute words that replace the vow word. ידות are incomplete phrases that still clearly point to a vow.

phrases.english: It is dealing with them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the ידות, the shortened vow phrases from the question in Steps 5 and 6.

phrases.english: and the text is missing something,
and this is what it is teaching:
All substitutes for vows are like vows,
and handles of vows are like vows.
phrases.notes: ידות literally means "handles": short phrases you can grab onto as a full vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions raised in Steps 5 and 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to talk only about כינויים, yet it gave an example of ידות with no rule about them
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read that both כינויים and ידות are like נדרים, so the ידות example has a rule behind it

steps.title: Why not explain the substitute words first?
steps.stepSummary: Since כינויים are mentioned first in the (filled-in) משנה, the משנה should explain them first, before it gives examples of ידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה explain the substitute words first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the filled-in text but now asks about the order. כינויים come first in the rule, so why does the משנה explain ידות first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you explain things in the same order you listed them. The filled-in משנה lists כינויים first and ידות second, but its examples start with ידות. The גמרא challenges this reversed order.

phrases.english: Then let it explain the substitutes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the משנה as filled in by Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of explanation in the filled-in משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items should be explained in the order they were listed, so כינויים should be explained before ידות

steps.title: The משנה explains the last item first
steps.stepSummary: It is the משנה's style to explain first whatever it mentioned last.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever the משנה ended with is what it explains first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה often explains the last item it mentioned first. ידות were mentioned last, so they are explained first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is not a mistake. It follows a known pattern: the משנה picks up right where it stopped and explains the last-mentioned item. The next step proves this pattern from other משניות.

keyTerms.meaning: That which it finished with; the last thing mentioned

phrases.english: That which it finished with,
that is what it explains first.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דְּסָלֵיק מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא מְפָרֵשׁ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.terutzResolutionType: A known style of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should explain items in the order it listed them
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה often explains the last-mentioned item first, so ידות come first

steps.title: Three examples from מסכת שבת
steps.stepSummary: Three משניות ask "what is allowed and what is not allowed," and each one starts by answering the second part, "what is not allowed."
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: With what may one light, and with what may one not light? One may not light with... In what may one insulate food, and in what may one not insulate it? One may not insulate with... With what may a woman go out, and with what may she not go out? A woman may not go out with...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three משניות to prove the pattern from Step 9. Each asks a two-part question and starts by answering the second part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the question first asks what is allowed, then what is not allowed. Yet each answer begins with what is not allowed, the part mentioned last. This shows that explaining the last item first is a normal style of the משנה, which supports the order in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
We insulate (wrap food to keep it hot)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה often explains the last item it mentioned first. That is why our משנה gives ידות examples before כינויים examples.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
With what may one light
and with what may one not light?
One may not light, etc.
In what may one insulate
and in what may one not insulate?
One may not insulate, etc.
With what may a woman go out
and with what may she not go out?
A woman may not go out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 9 with examples
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the משנה explains the last-mentioned item first
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three משניות in מסכת שבת (lighting, insulating, a woman going out), each of which answers "what is not allowed" first

steps.title: Many משניות explain the first item first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה really always explains the last item first. It quotes a משנה about inheritance that explains the first case first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that whatever the משנה opens with, it does not explain first? But we learned in a משנה: There are relatives who inherit and pass on inheritance, and relatives who inherit but do not pass on inheritance. And these are the ones who inherit and pass on inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 9. It brings a משנה in בבא בתרא that explains its first case first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the משנה's style is to explain the last item first. This משנה lists two groups and then goes straight to the first group, the one that inherits and passes on. So the 'last item first' rule does not seem to be the משנה's fixed style.

keyTerms.meaning: That it opened with, meaning what the משנה mentioned first
Those who pass on an inheritance to others

steps.confusionAlert: Read the opening line as a challenge, not a real question. The גמרא is saying: 'You claim the משנה never explains the first item first? Look at these משניות!'

phrases.english: And is it true that wherever it opens with something,
it does not explain that first?
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 9: the משנה explains the last-mentioned item first. Now the גמרא tests it.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
There are those who inherit and pass on an inheritance,
and those who inherit but do not pass on an inheritance.
And these are the ones who inherit and pass on an inheritance.
phrases.notes: Notice that it goes right back to the first group. That is the whole point of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּפָתַח לָא מְפָרֵשׁ בְּרֵישָׁא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the style rule from step 9, which step 10 had supported with proofs.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's style is to explain first whatever it mentioned last.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in בבא בתרא lists two cases and explains the first one first. So the claimed style is not consistent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בבא בתרא about who inherits and who passes on inheritance.

steps.title: Second example: Women permitted to husbands but forbidden to יבמים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יבמות also explains its first case first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are women who are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their יבמים, and women permitted to their יבמים and forbidden to their husbands. And these are the ones permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their יבמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second משנה to strengthen its challenge. This one is about יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two groups of women. It then explains the first group, permitted to husbands and forbidden to יבמים. This is another case of 'first item explained first,' which goes against step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers-in-law who would do יבום if the husband dies without children

phrases.english: There are women who are permitted to their husbands
and forbidden to their brothers-in-law,
and some permitted to their brothers-in-law but forbidden to their husbands.
And these are the ones permitted to their husbands
and forbidden to their brothers-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to the challenge begun in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge to the 'last item first' style rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יבמות about women permitted or forbidden to husbands and יבמים.

steps.title: Third and fourth examples: מנחות with oil, לבונה, הגשה and תנופה
steps.stepSummary: Two משניות in מנחות list two kinds of offerings and explain the first kind first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are offerings that need oil and frankincense, and some that need oil but not frankincense. And these are the ones that need oil and frankincense. There are offerings that need bringing near but not waving, and some that need waving but not bringing near. And these are the ones that need bringing near.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two more משניות, both about מנחות (flour offerings), to add to its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות open with two categories. Each one then explains the first category first: oil and לבונה in the first משנה, הגשה in the second. That makes four sources that go against the rule from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, placed on some flour offerings
Bringing the offering near to the corner of the מזבח

phrases.english: There are some that require oil and frankincense,
and some that require oil but not frankincense.
And these are the ones that require oil and frankincense.
There are some that require bringing near
and do not require waving,
and some that require waving but not bringing near.
And these are the ones that require bringing near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and fourth source to the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge to the 'last item first' style rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two משניות in מנחות about oil and לבונה, and about הגשה and תנופה.

steps.title: Fifth example: A firstborn for inheritance but not for the כהן
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in בכורות also explains its first case first. This finishes the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a firstborn for inheritance who is not a firstborn for the כהן, and a firstborn for the כהן who is not a firstborn for inheritance. And who is a firstborn for inheritance but not a firstborn for the כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings its fifth and last source, a משנה about a בכור. Here the challenge ends, and the גמרא will need to answer it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two kinds of בכור. It then asks about the first kind first, the firstborn for inheritance. With five משניות all opening with their first item, the style rule from step 9 looks seriously shaken.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn for inheritance, who gets a double share
A firstborn for the כהן, who must be redeemed through פדיון הבן

steps.whatToRemember: Five משניות (בבא בתרא, יבמות, מנחות twice, בכורות) explain their FIRST item first. That directly challenges the idea from step 9 that the משנה explains the last item first. The next step answers this challenge.

phrases.english: There is one who is a firstborn for inheritance
but is not a firstborn for the priest,
and one who is a firstborn for the priest but not a firstborn for inheritance.
And who is a firstborn for inheritance
but not a firstborn for the priest?!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בְּכוֹר לְנַחֲלָה וְאֵין בְּכוֹר לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the fifth and final source to the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge to the 'last item first' style rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורות about a firstborn for inheritance and a firstborn for the כהן.

steps.title: When there are many cases, the משנה starts with the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משניות from the challenge list many cases, so they explain the first one first. When there are only two items, the משנה explains the last one first.
steps.simpleTranslation: These משניות have many cases, so they explain the one they mentioned first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last few steps. It says those משניות are a different kind of case because they list many items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 9 is narrowed: a משנה explains the last item first only when it has just two items. When a משנה lists many items, it is natural to go in order and start from the first. This saves the original rule while explaining all the sources quoted against it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are many; there are many cases

phrases.english: These, because they have many cases,
phrases.notes: "These" means the משניות quoted in steps 11-14, about inheritance, יבמות, מנחות and בכורות.

phrases.english: it explains the one it opened with first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built up in steps 11-14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a list of many cases versus a list of only two items.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה always explains the last item first, so the sources that explain the first item first would contradict that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'last item first' style applies only when there are two items. Lists of many cases go in order from the first.

steps.title: A משנה about animals on שבת has only two sides but starts with the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the משנה in שבת about what an animal may go out with has only two sides, yet it starts by explaining the first side (what is allowed).
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה "With what may an animal go out and with what may it not go out" does not have many cases, and it teaches first: a camel goes out (with a halter).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings a משנה with only two sides that still explains the first side first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 15, a משנה with only two items should explain the last item first. The משנה in שבת asks "what is allowed" and "what is not allowed," and then opens with the allowed side: a camel may go out. This seems to break the rule even after it was narrowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out (into the public area on שבת)

phrases.english: But there is "With what may an animal go out
and with what may it not go out"
which does not have many cases,
and it teaches: "A camel goes out"!
phrases.notes: That is the allowed side, which is the first part of the opening question.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בַּמֶּה בְּהֵמָה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just made in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 15 that only lists of many cases explain the first item first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in שבת has only two sides, so by step 15 it should start with the last side. Instead it starts with the first side, what is allowed.
